title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0RC1RD_1LA1RA_1LE0LE_1RF0LA_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0RC1RD_1LA1RA_1LE0LE_1RF0LA_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, but the whole map is now known and no halt is in sight. Sample the run when the head is in state D at the left end: the tape is DL(m, T) = D> 1 00 (10)^m T with a short tail word T. One round multiplies m by 4/3 and rewrites T; for m ≥ 30 it depends on m only through m mod 3, so the round map (m, T) → ((4m + c(r,T))/3, τ(r,T)) is computed exactly from small representatives. It matches every DL event of the direct run up to 5·109 steps and was iterated for 100,000 rounds (past 1024990 steps) without a halt. The P-map of the first analysis (T = 1) is proved in Lean for every n. No (residue, tail) pair met so far, among 90,000 explored, halts.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 46,085 cells have been visited and 26,884 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.079).

claims.title: The P-map, for every n
claims.text: With P(n) = (101)^n 01 A> and Q(n) = (101)^n 110101 A>: P(3k) → P(4k+2) in 27k²+87k+35 steps, P(3k+1) → P(4k+3) in 27k²+105k+62, P(3k+2) → Q(4k+4) in 27k²+123k+117, for all k. Built from five generated rules (the D-loop, iterated by induction, and the right sweep) .

claims.title: Blank tape to the first excursion
claims.text: The machine reaches P(1) after 14 steps and then, through P(3), 6, 10, 15, 22, 31, 43, 59, the excursion start Q(80) after exactly 27,264 steps.

claims.title: The round map matches the direct run
claims.text: DL(m, T) = D> 1 00 (10)^m T (head at the left end). Every one of the 31 DL events of the direct C run up to 5·109 steps is the one the round map predicts, step count included.

claims.title: A round depends on m only mod 3
claims.text: For each (r, tail) pair used, four representatives m = 3j + r (j = 10..13) give the same tail τ(r,T), the same c = 3m' − 4m and a step count quadratic in j; the iteration relies on this. A Lean proof would state each round with symbolic k (the D-loop lemma already allows any tail).

claims.title: 100,000 rounds without a halt
claims.text: Iterating the round map from blank tape: 100,000 rounds, the last one beyond 10<sup>24990</sup> steps, m ≈ 10<sup>12494</sup>; the tail returns to T = 1 in 9,214 rounds and is never longer than 106 cells; 18,555 (residue, tail) pairs are used.

claims.title: No halting round is known at all
claims.text: The tail behaves like a recurrent random process (driven by m mod 3, which is pseudo-random) on a language of block lists. Exploring the tail graph breadth-first with every residue allowed (30,000 tails, 90,000 rounds) finds no round that halts. So a halt is not merely unlikely: no reachable way to halt is known; this hints at an invariant that a stronger decider could prove.

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m mod 3) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (30 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 21 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 309,710 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 14,535 of the run (A = 10, U = 01, m = 88, B = (empty)): 309,710 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 128,548 bits (about 1077,393 steps of the machine). 29,114 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 120 cells.

claims.title: No halting class among 5,000 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 9,484 found, to depth 13. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not proved either way. The round map is a finite-state rewrite of the tail word, so a proof of non-halting would be an invariant on the tail language that excludes the halting pattern (D reading 0 with a 0 on its left).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but its map is now fully known. A block of 101s grows by 4/3 each round, while a short word at the right end, the tail, gets rewritten; the machine could only stop inside such a rewrite, and none of the 90,000 rewrites tried stops.

facts.text: The 4/3 map on (101)^n 01 is proved in Lean for every n.
100,000 rounds of the exact round map without a halt.
None of 90,000 explored (residue, tail) rounds halts.

sections.heading: A 4/3 counter and a tail
html: Look at the tape whenever the head is at its left end in state D. It always reads 1 00 (10)^m T: a long run of m copies of 10 and then a short tail word T. Between two such moments (a round) the head:

1. sweeps right, turning every three 10 into two 101 (the same length, 6 cells);
  2. runs into the tail and rewrites it, a few cells at a time;
  3. comes back and, one 101 at a time, carries the 101 block back to the left end as pairs of 10 (the D-loop, which walks to the left end and back for every copy, so a round costs about 3m² steps).
Net effect: m grows by a factor 4/3 each round, and the tail changes. Which change happens depends only on the tail and on the remainder of m mod 3.

With the tail 1 this is the P-map of the first analysis: P(n) = (101)^n 01 A> is the moment just before DL(2n+1, 1).

sections.heading: A word that wanders and comes back
html: The tails are lists of small blocks separated by runs of zeros, like (010)^3 0^4 (10)^2 1 or 1^2 (01)^6. Because m mod 3 behaves like a coin with three sides, the tail does a random walk among these words: from blank tape it is back to 1 in 9,214 of the first 100,000 rounds, and it is never longer than 106 cells.

The round map is exact: a round depends on m only through m mod 3 (checked on four values of m for every tail used), so a round with an m of twelve thousand digits is computed from one with m ≈ 30. It agrees with every event of the direct simulation up to 5·109 steps.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The machine halts exactly when state D reads a 0 that has another 0 to its left (D writes 1, E steps left onto the 0, F steps back onto the new 1 and has no rule). That can only happen while a tail is being rewritten. Exploring every tail reachable from 1 breadth first, with all three remainders allowed at every round (90,000 rounds in all), not one round halts. So the run is probviously non-halting, and more: no way to halt is known at all, which suggests an invariant waiting to be found.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: The kernel checks the P-map for every n: P(3k) → P(4k+2), P(3k+1) → P(4k+3), P(3k+2) → (101)^(4k+4) 110101 A>, with exact step counts, and the run from blank tape to that first excursion (27,264 steps). The D-loop lemma holds with any tail to its right, so the remaining step to a full proof of a round is the right sweep through each tail, stated with a symbolic k.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state D reading 1 with only 0s to its left. Read rightwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m mod 3) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 21 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 14,535 of the run (A = 10, U = 01, m = 88, B = (empty)): 309,710 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 128,548 bits (about 1077,393 steps of the machine). 29,114 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 120 cells.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 5,000 contexts expanded, 9,484 found, to depth 13. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.079).
After 109 steps the tape spans 46,085 cells (33,996 left of the start, 124 right), with a density of 1s of 0.583.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: 4/3 map on (101)^n with a tail word transformed each round (finite-state rounds)
summary: Each round multiplies a block of (101)s by 4/3 and rewrites a short tail word; the round depends on n only mod 3, so the map is exact and iterated 100,000 rounds (past 10^24990 steps) without a halt; the P-map is proved in Lean for all n.
